questions.question: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of symmetric key cryptography compared to asymmetric key cryptography.
questions.solution_html:
• asymmetric key cryptography? U/CO3
  • Symmetric key cryptography
  • Advantage Disadvantage
  • Speed and efficiency: It is much faster than
  • asymmetric methods because its algorithms are
  • less computationally intensive. This makes it ideal
  • for encrypting large amounts of data like files
  • databases, and VPNs.
  • Key distribution c hallenge: The secret key must be
  • securely shared between the sender and receiver before
  • communication can begin. This can be difficult
  • especially with many participants, and is a major
  • security vulnerability.
  • Simplicity: It is simpler to implement and
  • requires less computational power.
  • Scalability issues: For every new communication pair
  • a unique key is needed. This creates a scalability
  • problem, as the number of keys required increases
  • dramatically with the number of users.
  • Lower overhead: The smaller ciphertext size and
  • faster processing make it more resource-efficient.
  • Lack of non-repudiation: Since both parties have the
  • same key, it's difficult to prove who actually sent a
  • message.
  • Asymmetric key cryptography
  • Advantage Disadvantage
  • Simplified key distribution: A public key can be shared
  • openly with anyone, while the private key is kept secret
  • eliminating the need for a pre-shared secret.
  • Slower performance: It is significantly
  • slower than symmetric encryption due to its
  • more complex algorithms.
  • Enhanced security for key exchange: It provides a secure
  • way to exchange a symmetric key, which can then be used
  • for faster bulk data encryption in a hybrid system.
  • Higher computational overhead: The
  • computational resources required are much
  • greater than for symmetric methods.
  • Digital signatures and non -repudiation: It enables
  • digital signatures and it provides non-repudiation.
  • Larger key sizes: The keys used in
  • asymmetric cryptography are much larger
  • compared to symmetric keys.

questions.question: How do encryption and decryption work together to protect sensitive information?
questions.solution_html:
• Encryption and decryption work together by scrambling readable information into an
  • unreadable format using an algorithm and a unique key during encryption, and then using the
  • corresponding key to reverse the process back into its original, readable form during
  • decryption.This two-step process ensures that only authorized parties with the correct key can
  • access sensitive data, protecting it from interception and unauthorized access.
  • Encryption and Decryption work together to protect information
  • • Confidentiality: Encryption ensures that even if data is intercepted, it remains private because
  • only the correct key can decrypt it.
  • • Authentication and integrity : In some systems, like public -key cryptography, the
  • combination of a public key for encryption and a private key for decr yption helps verify that
  • the message came from the intended sender and hasn't been altered.
  • • Layered security: By encrypting data both "at rest" (when stored) and "in transit" (when being
  • sent), organizations add multiple layers of protection against theft and interception.
